questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The fact that it was in an English-speaking country and that I was able to get courses pre-approved.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had the best study abroad experience at University of Limerick! I can only recommend UL as a host university as the university offers a broad selection of opportunities for you to try out during your stay. Furthermore, Irish people are the most open-minded and welcoming people, and they are very easy to become friends with.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Once I was accepted at UL, the university sent a lot of emails with information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Firstly, the university offered a pick-up service from the airport directly to the university when the international students arrived, which was very convenient. In the first week, there was an introduction week where all the needed information about course registration, how to find your way around at the university, formal requirements, ect. was presented.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The international coordinators at UL are very friendly and ready to help you, and they answer emails very quickly if you have any questions before or upon arrival.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You can live in different kinds of student villages. The student villages vary in prize, type (apartments vs. houses) and the number of roommates.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There is a kitchen in every student accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Apply for on campus accommodation as soon as you get accepted at UL! Unfortunately, UL takes in more international student than they can accommodate on campus and the spots get filled up very early. Even though the on campus accommodation is quite expensive it is totally worth it to live close to the buildings where you have classes and to the places where all the activities take place.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived in Thomond Village and the facilities deserve 5/5 because you get a big room and your own bathroom. The only reason I rate it 4/5 is that it is very expensive (also the most expensive student village).

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very easy and the university offers you with all the information you need to register correctly.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: When you get accepted at UL you register online for ten modules but it is not guarantied that the modules will run, so the registration is not binding. You can find a book of modules with descriptions of the modules online at the university's website. In the first two weeks of your stay, you can attend all the lectures of the modules you consider taking. This gives you a chance to chose the modules you find the most interesting. After the two weeks, you fill in a blanket with the modules you want to take, get it signed by the Erasmus coordinator, and then upload it at "Sulis" (the UL version of Absalon).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus coordinators are always ready to help you. You can also always talk to the lectures if you have any questions about their module.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the modules I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Attend a lot of different lectures in the first two weeks! Some of the modules that you initially was planning on taking might not fulfil your expectations while others might surprise you. As a psychology student you can take modules from other faculties as electives which is a good opportunity to learn something different from what you are used to at your home university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The modules were interesting and the lecturers were very passionate. As an Erasmus student you are allowed to take modules from all years of the psychology undergraduate degree which expand the selection of psychology modules, but if you have to find certain modules (in relation to merit), as I had to, the selection of modules is quite narrow.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level is a bit lower than UCPH, but I did not find that this was a problem for my exchange experience.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The number of students at the lectures are way smaller which allows a lot more interaction both with the lecturer and with the other students. In general, the style of teaching is more personal and some of the lecturers even learn the names of the students in their module. However, the classes are not as critical as at UCPH, and some of the modules just go through the textbook material.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Advanced Research Methods, Developmetal Psychopathology, Abnormal and Clinical Psychology, Empirical Psychology and Sociology of Gender and Popular Culture.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sociology of Gender and Popular Culture! The lectures are very interesting with a high academic level, the assignments are challenging, and the lecturer is very passionate, communicative and entertaining.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I spent a lot of money on weekend trips around Ireland.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were cheaper than in Denmark, but beer and food on restaurants were almost the same.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UL offers a lot of different clubs and societies and a lot of sport facilities on campus including a gym (with free access if you live on campus), swimming pool, climbing wall, and a lot of different fields/pitches.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All you could wish for! There is a club or society for almost every interest you might have. Furthermore, the university arranged different kind of social and cultural events during the semester.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Make sure to join at least one club or society. I would highly recommend the Kayak Club (no previous kayak experience needed) or the Outdoor Pursuit Club, which offers both hiking, climbing, caving and orientering.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore beautiful Ireland! Go to Killarney National Park, Connemara National Park and Wicklow Mountains for beautiful hikes, Go to Dingle, Northern Ireland and the west coast in general for stunning nature spots, and go to Dublin, Cork, and Galway to explore other irish cities. Ireland has a car sharing system called GoCar where you can rent cars at a fair price even when you are under 25 years. This makes travelling around Ireland very easy.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The Irish people are the most friendly, welcoming and warm people you will ever meet.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club or society. This is the easiest way to become friends with the local students. Otherwise, try to make it to a house party in College Court ;)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people! As mentioned previously, the Irish people are the best.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Join a club or society as it is the best way to get to know some Irish students. The club members are very open to international students and the clubs offer a lot of social life. 2. Enjoy every day of your stay! You are only there for 4 months and time flies by so fast. 3. Make an effort to get Irish friends. They are very friendly, great fun and throw some wild parties.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try your best to get on campus accommodation as it will make the practicalities during your stay a lot easier.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social life with the other international students and the Irish students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The day when I had to leave, but once I arrived everything worked out perfectly.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Again, I would highly recommend the Kayak Club. The people are so nice and helpful and white water kayaking is so much fun!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
